title: Session entropy bucketization & resume protocol — scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, personal sketch for reducing session state fragmentation caused by small variations in client prompts and deterministic randomness (temperatures, top_k sampling seeds, system message micro-diffs). The core idea is to bucketize entropy-affecting inputs into coarse classes and persist a compact resume manifest so resumptions are both cheaper and more reproducible across client restarts and proxy hops.

Motivation / problem statement:
- In many realtime clients we see many near-duplicate sessions that diverge only by small random seeds or micro-edits in user instructions. That causes: expensive cold K/V cache misses, unnecessary recomputation of large prefix contexts, and poor hit rates for streaming resume.
- Current session checkpoint format (binary blob of KV cache + token index) is heavy and brittle to tiny prompt edits. We want something that: 1) improves cache hit rate across near-duplicates, 2) preserves fidelity for resume when it matters, 3) is small and easy for clients/proxies to store/forward.

High-level approach:
1) Classify inputs into deterministic classes along two axes: structural-content and entropy-profile.
   - structural-content: canonicalized system + user instruction hash (apply normalizations: whitespace, canonical punctuation, template variable removal)
   - entropy-profile: discrete bucket describing sampling configuration and expected stochastic variance (e.g., DETERMINISTIC / LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH).
2) Persist a Resume Manifest that references: canonicalized-content-id, entropy-bucket-id, last-token-index, small shard of compressed KV checkpoint (only top-N most frequently accessed KV entries), and a short provenance checksum.
3) On resume, runtime tries the following ordered fallback:
   a) exact manifest match (canonical content id + entropy bucket + token idx) -> direct restore using compressed shard + replay from token index
   b) cross-bucket tolerant match (same canonical content id, entropy bucket within one step) -> attempt partial restore, replay extra tokens with probability-aware adjustments (see heuristics)
   c) content-similarity match (loose similarity threshold on canonical content hash) -> choose largest overlapping KV shard, replay longer window, mark as approximate resume (telemetry + optional user-level flag)
   d) full cold-start if nothing suitable found.

API / Resume Manifest shape (text sketch):
- endpoint: POST /v1/sessions/:session_id/resume-manifest-apply
- headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, X-Client-Proto-Version: 1, X-Resume-Intent: try-tolerant
- request body (JSON):
  {
    "manifest_version": "1",
    "canonical_content_id": "sha256:...",
    "entropy_bucket": "MEDIUM",
    "last_token_idx": 2345,
    "kv_shard_refs": ["shard://kv/abc123:0-10240"],
    "provenance": "meta:prompt-template=v2;user-agent=android:5.6",
    "checksum": "sha256:..."
  }
- response body (JSON):
  {
    "result": "applied|approximate|cold_start",
    "restored_tokens": 124,
    "replay_hint": "start_from_token_index: 2345",
    "warnings": ["entropy-bucket-mismatch: HIGH->MEDIUM (increased randomness during replay)"]
  }

Entropy bucket config sketch (example values):
- DETERMINISTIC: temperature < 0.01, top_p ~0.0, sampling seed fixed -> resume requires minimal replay (deterministic replay)
- LOW: temperature < 0.4, top_p < 0.7 -> small nondeterminism, can trust short replay window (20-40 tokens) and reuse cached KV shard
- MEDIUM: temp 0.4-0.8, top_p 0.7-0.95 -> expect content drift, prefer larger shard + longer replay (50-200 tokens)
- HIGH: temp > 0.8 or explicit sampling modes -> treat as best-effort; manifest serves primarily for metadata and provenance, not exact restore

Heuristics for canonicalization (practical rules):
- Trim to N=8 canonical paragraphs of conversation; collapse repeated whitespace; remove benign indirections (e.g., timestamps, run-ids) using simple regex rules maintained in config file.
- For dialog-like sequences, only include last M turns (configurable by team/route). This balances between cacheability and fidelity.
- Maintain a small, versioned normalization pipeline on client and server to avoid divergence. Manifest includes normalization_version tag.

KV shard selection heuristic:
- Keep top-K most-hot key vectors (by access frequency during the session) when generating a shard. K configurable by deployment tier (e.g., K=64 for hosted, 256 for dedicated).
- Compress using delta-quant + zstd level 3; include small bloom filter for query membership to speed partial merges on server-side.

State machine ASCII (very rough):

  CLIENT (create manifest) --> [UPLOAD manifest] --> RUNTIME (store manifest + shard ref)
       |                                         ^
       | resume request                            |
       v                                         |
  CLIENT (resume) -> RUNTIME (match manifest?) -> if applied -> RETURN restored state
                          |-> if approximate -> RETURN with warnings + telemetry
                          |-> fallback cold-start -> compute new manifest

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to version normalization rules and migrate older manifests? Proposal: embed normalization_version in manifest; servers maintain compatibility layer for two previous versions only.
- Security: manifests expose canonical_content_id hashes — are they sensitive? Treat as normal metadata (not PII), but policies may require encryption at rest and ACL checks for cross-tenant shares.
- Client adoption: make client libs produce manifests automatically behind a flag; give SDKs a small local cache to store manifest+shard for instant resume when network flaky.
- Telemetry: track resume_success_rate, approximate_resume_rate, average_replay_tokens, CPU saved vs cold start. Add metric tags by entropy_bucket.

Implementation notes / dev plan (mini roadmap):
- Week 0-1: implement server-side manifest table + minimal apply/lookup API (no shard restoration yet).
- Week 2-3: client SDK: normalization + manifest emitter on session close; small binary shard writer for hot keys.
- Week 4: shard restore flow and heuristics for cross-bucket replay.
- Week 5+: field test on small tenant, gather telemetry, iterate on bucket thresholds.

Back-of-envelope economics:
- If we improve cache hit rate for near-duplicate sessions by 15% on a route that contributes 12% of token spend, expected token cost savings ~1.8% platform-wide (plausible to justify dedicated work).

Notes to self / reminders:
- Keep manifest intentionally small (<4KB) for mobile-friendly transfers.
- Avoid encoding full KV dumps in manifests; use shard refs into the object store.
- Add unit tests that simulate micro-edits to prompts and measure lookup fall-through behavior.

End of scratchpad.
